title: the isolation a create asks for
asserts: a create with isolateWorktree lands the session in a FRESH git worktree beside the repo - the pty's own cwd, not just a field in the meta - while a create without the flag runs in the directory it named, and a target that cannot be isolated is refused rather than started in the shared tree. Several agents are dispatched into one checkout at a time and the worktree is the only thing keeping them off each other's files, so a core that drops the flag and still answers `created` reports a success that did not happen.

steps.note: a sibling <repo>-worktrees/<name> tree, and worktreePath records what has to be removed later
the agent PROCESS is in the worktree: a core that reported the path but spawned in the repo would pass the meta assertion and fail here
no flag: the other half of the contract
the worktree appears because the frame asked for it, not because every create gets one
a target that is not a git repository at all
refused, not started unisolated: an agent loose in a shared checkout that was told it had its own is the bug this closes
